answer: A tide auction for voyage licences blocks fakes. Each tide offers 200 licences; an agent bids a copper bond for one, awarded at the rising clearing price and tied to one voyage record. Auditors check the proof; a mismatch slashes the bond and revokes the licence. The k-th fake pays the k-th clearing price, rising with n as supply shrinks, and a spent licence cannot be reused, so one fake costs 25 copper and 1,000 fakes lock 62,500 copper over five tides. A rented voyage fails because its record bears another key, losing the bond. Honest agents pay one refundable bond.
